statement:
Write down the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^n$, where $n$ is a positive integer.

(i) By substituting particular values of $x$, or otherwise, show that if $n$ is an even positive integer, then
$$\binom n0+\binom n2+\binom n4+\cdots+\binom nn=\binom n1+\binom n3+\cdots+\binom n{n-1}=2^{n-1}.$$

(ii) Show that if $n$ is any positive integer, then
$$\binom n1+2\binom n2+3\binom n3+\cdots+n\binom nn=n2^{n-1}.$$

Hence evaluate
$$\sum_{r=0}^{n}\bigl(r+(-1)^r\bigr)\binom nr.$$
solution:
The binomial expansion is
$$(1+x)^n=\sum_{r=0}^{n}\binom nr x^r.$$

(i) Substituting $x=1$:
$$2^n=\binom n0+\binom n1+\cdots+\binom nn. \tag{1}$$
Substituting $x=-1$ (with $n$ even):
$$0=\binom n0-\binom n1+\binom n2-\cdots-\binom n{n-1}+\binom nn. \tag{2}$$

Adding (1) and (2), then dividing by 2:
$$\binom n0+\binom n2+\cdots+\binom nn=2^{n-1}.$$
Subtracting (2) from (1), then dividing by 2:
$$\binom n1+\binom n3+\cdots+\binom n{n-1}=2^{n-1}.$$

(ii) Differentiate $(1+x)^n=\sum_{r=0}^n\binom nr x^r$ with respect to $x$:
$$n(1+x)^{n-1}=\sum_{r=1}^n r\binom nr x^{r-1}.$$
Substituting $x=1$:
$$n2^{n-1}=\binom n1+2\binom n2+3\binom n3+\cdots+n\binom nn.$$

Finally,
$$\sum_{r=0}^n(r+(-1)^r)\binom nr=\sum_{r=0}^n r\binom nr+\sum_{r=0}^n(-1)^r\binom nr.$$
The first sum is $n2^{n-1}$ (from (ii), noting the $r=0$ term is zero). The second is $(1-1)^n=0$ for $n\ge1$. Hence the value is $n2^{n-1}$.
hints: Substitute x=1 and x=-1 into (1+x)^n and combine.
For the weighted sum, differentiate the binomial expansion.
Split the final sum into the weighted part and the alternating part.
